items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen in walks of 10 to 19 minutes. In one study, walking after dinner was linked to a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in sugar.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: 40.0% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later. Across the program, sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners than after earlier ones in the same person, and 13.3 mg/dL more after a dinner at 8-9 pm than after one before 6 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a quarter of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: Eating dinner at 8 pm or later is linked to a rise in sugar, with dinners from 8-9 pm linked to a rise about 13.3 mg/dL more than dinners before 6 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it helps with sugar.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: In one study, adding an overnight fast to coaching changed some numbers by -0.03 points compared to coaching alone, but it's not clear if this applies to everyone. Your overnight fast averaged 6.6 hours, and it might be worth looking into longer fasts to see if they make a difference for you.
